classification: LOCAL PROVED SMOOTH IDENTITIES AND ALGEBRA
screened_candidate: Serre compensated integrability applied to the natural constant-density four-dimensional NS stress tensor, with and without viscous stress.
completed_scope: PTS.2-6: the complete viscous tensor has exact NS row divergence. Its Schur complement is (p+c)I-2nu D; the unshifted mean-zero periodic tensor is PSD only for constant solutions. The minimal time-only pressure shift is esssup_x(2nu lambda_max(D)-p), with no c-prime term.

PTS.7-8: the determinant removes explicit velocity, but not pressure/strain dependence. Its nonnegative cube root is at most p+c. No terminal-uniform pressure-shift estimate has been derived from basic energy.

PTS.9-13: deleting viscous stress leaves a real double-divergence/Hessian cancellation for arbitrary smooth solenoidal time curves with canonical Poisson pressure. This weaker identity alone cannot distinguish NS dynamics.

PTS.14-16: on a finite time interval and a full spatial torus, both direct averaged determinant outputs follow solely from Schur complements, trace/AM-GM and velocity covariance. No time periodicity, momentum equation or Serre theorem is used here.
PTS.17-18: retain the localized row-divergence and double-divergence product terms, including the factor2nu Delta u dot grad eta; endpoints and side traces are not removed.
limitations: Only these two natural tensors and their direct global-average outputs were screened. A local weighted or boundary estimate using the same tensor remains possible; no general positive-tensor impossibility theorem is claimed.

Smooth identities on compact preterminal intervals do not supply terminal-uniform bounds or automatic good scales for arbitrary original data. No actual NS cost-divergence counterexample was constructed.
Serre's upstream Monge-Ampere existence theory and all later extensions were not independently re-certified. No exhaustive novelty search or human peer review was performed.
This is an internal method-screen record, not a new independent research section, release, numerical example or theorem toward Clay.
